_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform — the STL ascii `any` mutation vocabulary and the reference implementation that exercises it. The shared stdio manifest already registers `stl-io` under the `stl-mesh` capability for creation/projection; that entry cannot cover mutation because it never declared the capability, so this subset registers its own oracle id against the SAME package for the `stl-ascii-mutate` capability instead of reusing the shared one (would fail the contract with oracle-capability-mismatch).

oracles.rationale: The reference binary/ASCII STL reader of the Rust ecosystem, used here to perform every declared `StlMutation` kind independently of this repository's own codec by round-tripping the triangle soup through `IndexedMesh`/`write_stl`. `stl_io` 0.8's own top-level doc comment states 'Writing is limited to binary STL' — confirmed in its source (`writer.rs` hardcodes a zeroed 80-byte header) — so it can express neither an ASCII body nor the solid name in either direction. `set-solid-name`, the one declared kind whose whole payload IS that name, is therefore applied as a direct ASCII header/trailer substitution on the same real document instead of routing through `stl_io`; the other 6 kinds round-trip through it unmodified. Comparison is projection-based (`semantic-mesh-v1`'s resolved-corner triangle soup), so the byte FORM the oracle emits never has to match the subject's own ASCII output.
